status: frozen dataset and claim scope for writeup consumers
selection_reason: Complete outcome-only rows and original metadata/raw-file recount support every cell; older KO grouping inputs are less complete. This choice replaces the older narrative as a unit.

arm_definition.candidate: agent.main dispatching rules_lucario; experimental Lucario player with project-authored KO intervention, distinct from entered unmodified tetsutani c61
arm_definition.OFF: Dedicated and broader KO switches absent in recorded environment.
arm_definition.ON: PTCG_MIRROR_PATCH_01_KO=1; +100000 score bonus for a projected knockout in the target scorer.

permitted_sentences: The same projected-knockout priority bonus produced opposite observed whole-game effects across seven tested opponent implementations.
In 8,400 recorded games, each opponent had 600 games per arm and 300 per seat, scoring a draw as half a win.
The ON-minus-OFF change was +14.33 percentage points against prvsiyan Static-Deck Tusk v24 and -11.58 points against penguin069 Public Scores 915.
Changes against aristophanivan 2plyexpectimax and pixiux Mega Lucario v62 were -7.42 and -7.75 points; the other three approximate intervals crossed zero.
These exploratory fixed-implementation comparisons do not justify a universal KO-priority default or establish which deck or decision caused the differences.

Older +12.33-point new-pilot result as a separate corroboration of an overlapping positive pool.
Older 20,400-game denominator, two-deck/two-pilot story or claimed deck discriminator.

Prospective prediction, proof that deck identity caused the signs, actual-knockout causal attribution, learned routing or general improvement to entered c61.
A guarantee that the scoring bonus makes every actual knockout outrank every alternative.
downstream_consumers: Canonical writeup body and its short KO paragraph

required_consumer_rule: Use this dataset, arms, all-seven supporting table and limitations together. Do not retain superseded figures, group labels, captions or citations. Two highlighted cells may illustrate the contrast only when the complete seven-cell table remains accessible.
limitations: Exploratory retrospective analysis of seven fixed opponent implementations. It is not a representative survey or a prospective prediction.

Intervals use independent-game sample-score variance and a 1.96 normal multiplier, with no multiplicity adjustment. Random-seed independence and absence of overdispersion are not established by these records.
All seven implementations are retained; interval crossings do not establish equivalence or no effect.
No decision traces accompany these rows. Individual knockout choices, mechanisms of losses and causal deck determination cannot be inferred.
No successful conditional selector, learned routing policy, student improvement or entered-player improvement is established.
Historical candidate runtime uses two Git commit labels with identical tracked agent tree and eval.py. This does not reconstruct untracked imports, engine bytes or every historical process.

Historical pool hash binds alias and selfcheck text, not opponent files. The full opponent main/deck hashes here were inspected from retained files on 2026-09-12; they are not a historical execution attestation.

The related preregistration describes 4,000 games per arm against c61 followed conditionally by a 300-per-arm panel. These recovered records instead contain 600 per arm in seven cells; no prospective status is claimed.
This dataset is separate from the older KO grouping studies, conditional KO-race follow-up, and the counter experiment that also has 8,400 records.
